problem: Image editing methods struggle with complex Human-Object Interactions (HOI) because existing benchmarks conflate HOI with static attributes and lack metrics that simultaneously assess interaction validity and human-object pair preservation.
approach: Introduce HOI-Edit benchmark with three cognitive levels and HOI-Eval metric using VLM Q&A. Propose SCPE (Self-Correcting Process Editing), which leverages Image-to-Video models' temporal generation to reframe editing as dynamic interaction remodeling, using iteratively refined prompts for self-correction.
contribution: SCPE achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art editing models on HOI-Edit by exploiting I2V models' temporal capabilities and providing interpretable failure diagnostics via video replay.

problem: Physics foundation models must solve PDEs in real-time while preserving physical conservation laws and generalizing to unseen geometries, but current approaches struggle to maintain accuracy under domain adaptation.
approach: Introduce Geo-NeWF (General-Geometry Neural Whitney Forms), which jointly learns a differential operator and reduced finite element spaces grounded in underlying geometry. Use Finite Element Exterior Calculus to exactly preserve conservation laws and transformer-based encoding to connect geometry and boundary conditions.
contribution: Geo-NeWF achieves state-of-the-art performance on steady-state PDE benchmarks and significantly improves generalization to out-of-distribution geometries compared to conventional baselines.

problem: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often fail under distribution shift because decisions depend on spurious visual correlations rather than task-relevant causal features.
approach: Formulate visual-action attribution as interventional estimation. Introduce Interventional Significance Score (ISS), an interventional masking procedure to estimate causal influence of visual regions on actions, and Nuisance Mass Ratio (NMR), a scalar measure of task-irrelevant attribution.
contribution: NMR predicts generalization behavior across diverse manipulation tasks, and ISS yields more faithful explanations than existing interpretability methods, providing a diagnostic approach for identifying causal misalignment in embodied policies.

problem: Motion-language retrieval methods focus on global alignment between entire motion sequences and textual representations, overlooking fine-grained interactions between local motion segments and individual body joints with text tokens.
approach: Propose Pyramidal Shapley-Taylor (PST) learning framework inspired by human motion perception, decomposing motion into temporal segments and spatial body joints. Learn cross-modal correspondences through progressive joint-wise and segment-wise alignment in a pyramidal fashion.
contribution: PST significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmark datasets by capturing both local semantic details and hierarchical structural relationships in motion-language correspondences.

problem: Multi-round human-AI collaboration lacks principled frameworks to ensure interactions reliably improve decision quality while avoiding harm to human strengths and adding value where humans err.
approach: Adopt human-centric view governed by counterfactual harm and complementarity principles, formalized via user-defined rules. Introduce online, distribution-free algorithm with finite-sample guarantees that enforces user-specified constraints over collaboration dynamics.
contribution: The online procedure maintains prescribed counterfactual-harm and complementarity violation rates under non-stationary interaction dynamics, with tightening constraints producing predictable shifts in human accuracy.

problem: Low-dimensional structures in eigenspectra of deep-learning matrices remain unexplained by theoretical advances that either capture only subsets of behavior or rely on impractical assumptions.
approach: Use unconstrained feature models (UFMs) to explain bulk-outlier structure in canonical deep-learning matrices (Hessian, gradients, weights). Show that Deep Neural Collapse (DNC) is the source of low-dimensional eigenspectra, with eigenvalues and eigenvectors constructable from feature means.
contribution: Provides unifying analytic explanation for wide range of spectral phenomena in deep learning, including detailed eigenvector analysis beyond empirical eigenvalue characterizations, validated on both linear/ReLU networks and standard architectures.

problem: Deep visual features lack task-aligned tolerance boundaries in feature space, making it difficult to control feature quality and understand maximum imperceptible distortion under constrained resources.
approach: Propose FeatJND, a task-aligned Just Noticeable Difference formulation that predicts maximum tolerable per-feature perturbation while preserving downstream task performance. Validate across image classification, detection, and instance segmentation with an estimator at standardized split points.
contribution: FeatJND-based distortions consistently preserve higher task performance than unstructured perturbations and enable token-wise dynamic quantization with clear gains over random/uniform step-size allocation.

problem: Large-scale LLM pretraining with 100k+ GPUs faces node failures that dominate wall-clock training time, requiring fault-tolerance mechanisms designed for restart-dominant regimes.
approach: Propose SPARe (Stacked Parallelism with Adaptive Reordering), which masks node failures during gradient synchronization by stacking redundant data shards across parallelism groups and adaptively reordering execution.
contribution: SPARe achieves availability comparable to traditional replication with only 2-3x computation overhead even at high redundancy, reducing time-to-train by 40-50% compared to traditional replication at 600k GPUs.

problem: Noise correlation-based credit assignment methods scale poorly because estimating the Jacobian requires perturbations scaling with network size, and isotropic noise conflicts with neural activity lying on low-dimensional manifolds.
approach: Propose Neural Manifold Noise Correlation (NMNC) that performs credit assignment using perturbations restricted to the neural manifold. Show theoretically and empirically that the Jacobian row space aligns with the neural manifold and manifold dimensionality scales slowly.
contribution: NMNC substantially improves performance and sample efficiency over vanilla noise correlation on CNNs, ImageNet models, and RNNs, and yields representations more similar to primate visual system than vanilla noise correlation.

problem: Training Meta-learning for Training-data Selection (MTS) often underperforms because of poor gradient signal-to-noise ratio causing optimization difficulties and lack of informative features correlating with data quality.
approach: Analyze MTS via normalized data weights to reveal dynamics and relationship between disparate data quality and poor GSNR. Propose increasing batch size to improve signal-to-noise, and introduce informative features capturing training data positions in distributions and training dynamics.
contribution: Simple solution of increasing batch size plus feature engineering yields average gains of 5.49% over training without selection and 2.89% over strongest baseline across four benchmarks.

problem: Language agents struggle to utilize past experience for test-time adaptation in dynamic conditions because most memory systems restrict retrieval to episode initiation, forcing reliance on static guidance.
approach: Propose Adaptive Memory Agent (AdaMEM) with hybrid memory architecture: maintains long-term trajectory memory of offline experiences while generating dynamic short-term strategy memory on-the-fly. Develop Step-wise Memory Fine-Tuning to synthesize high-quality strategies from retrieved experiences.
contribution: AdaMEM achieves up to 13% gains on ALFWorld, 11% on WebShop, and consistent leading performance on HotpotQA, enabling continuous reasoning and self-evolution post-deployment.

problem: Surrogate loss functions face a fundamental trade-off: smooth losses enable fast optimization but yield slow consistency bounds, while piecewise-linear losses achieve optimal rates but are non-differentiable.
approach: Introduce Linear-Core (LC) Surrogates by stitching linear core to smooth tail, creating differentiable loss functions (C1 and C2) that retain strict linear H-consistency bounds across binary classification, multi-class, and structured prediction.
contribution: First explicit construction simultaneously achieving smoothness and linear H-consistency rates. Multi-class version shows 2.6% improvement on corrupted CIFAR-10; structured prediction variant yields 23x speedup over Structured SVMs on large-vocabulary sequence tagging.

problem: Scalability of Large Language Models to long sequences is hindered by quadratic cost of self-attention and limitations of positional encodings.
approach: Introduce Caracal, which replaces self-attention with parameter-efficient O(L log L) Multi-Head Fourier (MHF) module. Apply frequency-domain causal masking via asymmetric padding and truncation for autoregressive capabilities. Use standard library operators for portability.
contribution: Caracal performs competitively with Transformer and SSM baselines while offering scalable and simple long-sequence modeling without hardware-specific implementations.

problem: Spherical vision transformers implementing local self-attention on spherical grids retain only partial SO(3) equivariance and rely on location-dependent positional embeddings that degrade robustness to camera tilt and object reorientation.
approach: Propose Spherical SO(3)-Equivariant Local Attention (SoLA), an LPE-free mechanism using distance-preserving positional modulation coupling query/key features with unit direction vectors via outer-product. Offers softmax-free linear variant computing attention via key-value aggregation.
contribution: SoLA achieves full SO(3) equivariance and substantially improves robustness to arbitrary 3D rotations compared to prior spherical transformers on 360° depth estimation and semantic segmentation.

problem: Stochastic optimization with Markovian noise and zero-order oracle presents challenges when mixing time is large, making expensive first-order oracles inefficient.
approach: Present derivative-free method for strongly convex smooth and non-smooth settings with one-point and two-point feedback oracles. Use randomized batching scheme where convergence estimates independent of mixing time tau when tau < dimension d.
contribution: Zero-order oracle approach more efficient than first-order oracle when mixing time less than dimension; complementary lower bounds confirm optimality of results.

problem: Deep learning for human sensing on edge systems is hindered by limited sensor data availability, resource constraints, and high costs of model development and deployment across different sensing modalities.
approach: Propose XTransfer, a modality-agnostic few-shot model transfer method with: (i) model repairing that safely mitigates modality shift by adapting pre-trained layers with minimal data, and (ii) layer recombining that efficiently searches and recombines layers in layer-wise manner.
contribution: XTransfer achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing sensor data collection costs, model training time, and edge deployment footprint across diverse human sensing datasets.

problem: LLMs relying on long chains of thought improve accuracy but incur substantial inference costs, and existing sequence-level reward-shaping methods offer limited control over how reasoning effort is allocated across tokens.
approach: Propose IAPO, an information-theoretic post-training framework assigning token-wise advantages based on each token's conditional mutual information with final answer. Identify informative reasoning steps while suppressing low-utility exploration.
contribution: IAPO improves reasoning accuracy while reducing reasoning length by up to 36%, outperforming token-efficient RL methods. Theory shows IAPO induces monotonic reductions in verbosity without harming correctness.

problem: Incorporating textual information into time-series forecasting faces a fundamental modality gap: text expresses temporal impacts implicitly and qualitatively while forecasting requires explicit quantitative signals.
approach: Propose TESS (Temporal Evolution Semantic Space) introducing interpretable, numerically grounded temporal primitives (distribution shift, volatility, shape, lag) extracted from text by LLM via structured prompting. Filter via confidence-aware gating as intermediate bottleneck.
contribution: TESS achieves up to 29% reduction in forecasting error compared to unimodal and multimodal baselines by bridging modality gap via semantic primitives.

problem: Traditional neural topic models optimize by reconstructing Bag-of-Words representations, overlooking contextual information and struggling with data sparsity.
approach: Introduce novel framework Distilling Soft Labels (DSL) from Language Models, projecting next-token probabilities from specialized prompts onto vocabulary and training topic models to reconstruct soft labels using LM hidden states.
contribution: DSL achieves substantial improvements in topic coherence and assignment accuracy, significantly outperforming baselines in identifying semantically similar documents for retrieval-oriented applications.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for forensics can capture semantic-level inconsistencies but lack ability to perceive low-level generator artifacts without sacrificing pre-trained semantic knowledge.
approach: Conduct layer-wise analysis revealing semantic information in early-to-middle layers and artifact-learning causes semantic forgetting. Propose Deep-VRM injecting artifact-specific signals as residual path into intermediate layer, preserving early semantic processing.
contribution: Deep-VRM achieves state-of-the-art across all forensic detection benchmarks by jointly modeling semantic reasoning and signal-level forensic cues, adaptively leveraging different forensic signal levels.

problem: Learning representations on continuous-time dynamic graphs is challenged by long-range information propagation; existing approaches capture only local temporal neighborhoods and fail on multi-hop or global structural patterns.
approach: Derive parameter-efficient state-space modeling framework for continuous-time dynamic graphs (CTDG-SSM). Introduce Continuous-time Topology-Aware HiPPO (CTT-HiPPO) reformulating HiPPO via Laplacian polynomial to encode temporal dynamics and graph structure jointly.
contribution: CTDG-SSM achieves state-of-the-art on dynamic link prediction, node classification, and sequence classification with large gains on datasets requiring long-range temporal and spatial reasoning.

problem: Diversity of robot embodiments and action spaces makes it challenging to build robot world models that generalize across different embodiments.
approach: Introduce Latent Action-Conditioned Robot World Model (LAC-WM) operating within learned unified latent action space shared across diverse embodiments. Compare with Explicit Action-Conditioned World Model (EAC-WM) conditioning on explicit motion labels.
contribution: LAC-WM improves performance over EAC-WM by up to 46.7% on dexterous manipulation and 11.7% on LIBERO. Unified latent action space enables downstream performance scaling positively with pretraining embodiments, unlike EAC-WM.

problem: LLM routing methods assume fixed quality and cost per LLM for each query, ignoring that same LLM's quality varies with output length, missing opportunities for cost-efficient high-quality configurations.
approach: Introduce R2-Router treating output length budget as controllable variable, jointly selecting best LLM and length budget via length-constrained instructions. Construct R2-Bench, routing dataset capturing LLM behavior across diverse output length budgets.
contribution: R2-Router achieves state-of-the-art performance at 4-5x lower cost than existing routers by treating routing as reasoning with deliberate exploration of LLM-length configurations.

problem: Evaluating Large Language Models requires prohibitive full-scale benchmarking, and existing coreset methods must estimate reliable item profiles from small source pools, becoming statistically unstable with newly released benchmarks.
approach: Introduce RepCore which aligns heterogeneous hidden states into unified latent space for coreset construction. Use subsets for performance extrapolation, leveraging information in hidden states beyond discrete correctness labels.
contribution: RepCore achieves precise estimation accuracy with as few as ten source models across five benchmarks and over 200 models. Spectral analysis reveals aligned representations separate broad response tendencies from task-specific reasoning.

problem: Functional calcium trace analysis remains task-specific with limited transfer across neuroscience objectives due to lack of large-scale pre-training frameworks.
approach: Propose CalM, self-supervised neural foundation model on neuronal calcium traces using high-performance tokenizer mapping traces to discrete vocabulary and dual-axis autoregressive transformer modeling neural and temporal dependencies.
contribution: CalM outperforms specialized baselines on neural population dynamics forecasting after pretraining and achieves superior behavior decoding results. Linear analyses reveal interpretable functional structures beyond predictive accuracy.

problem: Density-based anomaly detection methods provide accurate predictions but performance severely degrades from inherent noise in data such as environmental or background noise.
approach: Present Noise-Robust Density Estimation (NRDE) learning Jacobian-regularized normalizing flow to estimate data sources while isolating noise. Categorize sources into pure-data and noise groups for robust anomaly detection.
contribution: NRDE provides theoretical support for effectiveness and outperforms 17 baselines on 47 benchmark datasets across vanilla anomaly detection, anomaly with contamination, noisy data, and transductive settings.

problem: Federated Graph Learning performance is hindered by graph-specific heterogeneity from divergent node feature distributions and disparate graph structures; existing methods overlook structural knowledge's role.
approach: Propose Fed-Kalter integrating Kalman filtering into graph neural networks. Introduce Kalter-Conv grounded in Kalman framework with learnable dynamics, treating structural embeddings as latent states and feature-augmented neighborhoods as noisy observations.
contribution: Fed-Kalter consistently outperforms state-of-the-art FGL methods on 16 graph classification datasets across 4 domains while enabling effective knowledge transfer and local personalization.

problem: LLMs in medical question-answering exhibit high reasoning capacity but produce hallucinations and outdated knowledge, and existing RAG methods rely on noisy token-level signals lacking multi-round refinement.
approach: Propose MA-RAG (Multi-Round Agentic RAG) iteratively evolving external evidence and reasoning history within agentic loop. Transform semantic conflict among candidate responses into actionable queries and optimize history traces.
contribution: MA-RAG surpasses inference-time scaling and RAG baselines, delivering substantial +6.8 points average accuracy on 7 medical Q&A benchmarks by leveraging inconsistency as proactive signal for multi-round reasoning.

problem: Personalizing AI decision support for heterogeneous human decision-makers in human-AI collaboration remains challenging when AI provides prediction sets and human makes final decision.
approach: Formulate personalization as contextual bandit with individual/task features as context, significance levels as arms via conformal prediction. Introduce AGCB framework exploiting continuity and monotonicity structural assumptions avoiding global function approximation.
contribution: AGCB achieves minimax-optimal dependence on learning horizon T via data-driven Zooming Mechanism and directional counterfactual information, showing strongest performance on heterogeneous data-scarce settings.

problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models suffer from expert overlap where different experts process similar tokens and learn redundant functions, resulting in ambiguous routing and underutilized capacity.
approach: Propose two plug-and-play auxiliary losses: intra-layer specialization loss penalizing cosine similarity between experts' SwiGLU activations, and cross-layer dependency loss maximizing joint Top-k routing probabilities across layers.
contribution: Both losses orthogonal to load-balancing and compatible with various MoE architectures, yielding consistent task gains, higher expert specialization, lower-entropy routing, and faster inference via stable expert pathways.

problem: Current benchmarks for generalist models largely overlook time series reasoning, a fundamental skill for complex problems ranging from energy management to traffic control.
approach: Introduce TSRBench, comprehensive multi-modal benchmark with 4125 problems from 14 domains across 4 dimensions: Perception, Reasoning, Prediction, Decision-Making. Evaluate over 30 LLMs, VLMs, and TSLLMs.
contribution: TSRBench reveals scaling laws hold for perception/reasoning but break for prediction, strong reasoning doesn't guarantee accurate forecasting, and multimodal models fail to effectively fuse text/visual time series despite complementary nature.

problem: Training agents to navigate uncertainty over long horizons requires effective credit assignment for intermediate progress, and outcome-based rewards alone are insufficient.
approach: Propose Delta-Belief-RL leveraging language model's intrinsic beliefs to reward intermediate progress via change in probability assigned to target solution. Train on synthetic interaction data to teach information-seeking.
contribution: Delta-Belief-RL consistently outperforms purely outcome-based RL rewards and generalizes to out-of-distribution applications from customer service to personalization. Performance improves beyond training horizon, increasing interaction-efficiency on Pass@k.

problem: Cosine similarity estimation in coarse-to-fine retrieval pipelines relies on sign-based sketches with structural variance peaks near 90°, where candidate selection is most difficult.
approach: Propose QA-Cos, query-aware decoder-side estimator treating sign bits as probabilistic observations rather than deterministic votes, departing from Hamming-agreement paradigm.
contribution: QA-Cos reduces estimation error by 15-20% in near-orthogonal region, improving Hit@K by ~30 percentage points at fixed budgets and reducing candidates by 45-50% at fixed recall in two-stage ANN pipelines.

problem: Watermarking of panoramic imagery is fundamentally challenged by arbitrary 3D rotations where conventional planar representations and augmentation-based strategies lack theoretical guarantees.
approach: Formulate panoramas as spherical signals leveraging SO(3) representation theory to derive provably rotation-invariant descriptors. Introduce third-order invariant construction coupling higher-order SO(3) irreducible representations via tensor products.
contribution: Spherical invariant bispectrum preserves phase information while remaining strictly rotation-invariant, enabling reliable watermark extraction under arbitrary 3D rotations with near-perfect robustness and high visual fidelity.

problem: Recent multi-modal time series models claim high performance on complex reasoning tasks but skip foundational evaluations of basic ability to describe structural properties of time series.
approach: Propose BEDTime benchmark assessing whether models can recognize, differentiate, and generate descriptions of univariate time series. Create five datasets reformatted across three modalities with robustness tests.
contribution: Evaluating 17 state-of-the-art models shows: dedicated time series-language models underperform, vision-language models surprisingly capable, language-only methods worst, and all approaches fragile to real-world robustness tests.

problem: Understanding anatomical shape evolution in response to developmental covariates requires quantifying spatially-varying uncertainties, but existing time-warping approaches ignore spatially heterogeneous dynamics.
approach: Introduce PRISM bridging implicit neural representations with uncertainty-aware statistical shape analysis. Model conditional distribution of shapes given covariates with closed-form Fisher Information metric.
contribution: PRISM provides spatially continuous estimates of population mean and covariate-dependent uncertainty with analytically tractable local temporal uncertainty quantification, demonstrating strong performance on shape evolution, anomaly detection, and interpretable uncertainty.

problem: Predicting outputs in non-Euclidean spaces (distributions, networks, matrices) with high-dimensional multivariate inputs faces curse of dimensionality while requiring interpretability.
approach: Propose DeSI (Deep Single-Index Fréchet Regression), semiparametric framework assuming single-index structure for conditional Fréchet mean. Estimate interpretable index direction using deep neural network, perform Fréchet regression on one-dimensional index.
contribution: DeSI mitigates curse of dimensionality while retaining interpretability. Provides theoretical guarantees including uniform approximation and convergence rates with strong predictive performance on distributions, networks, and positive-definite matrices.

problem: Small models with latent recursion achieve promising results on reasoning tasks but recursive steps often don't effectively contribute to depth, resulting in dead compute.
approach: Analyze algorithms that latent reasoning provides by formalizing it as classifier-free guidance and policy improvement algorithm. Propose training schemes from RL and diffusion methods for latent reasoning models.
contribution: Using RL/diffusion training on Tiny Recursive Model avoids dead compute steps and reduces forward passes by 18x while maintaining performance. Policy improvement perspective explains recursive behavior.

problem: Instruction tuning for speech language models is substantially more challenging than text LLMs as it requires learning new modality and wide range of speech-specific instructions at scale.
approach: Propose SpeechCombine, instruction-following SLM without explicit instruction tuning using only single round of speech pre-training on 30k hours. Directly combine weights of speech-adapted model with weight difference between instruction-tuned and base text LLM.
contribution: Simple weight combination preserves original text LLM knowledge while effectively transferring to speech domain, suggesting new SLM training direction avoiding massive speech data requirements.

problem: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research agents follow linear or outline-centric planning, suffering from lost-in-the-middle failures or weak supervision for identifying missing relations and triggering targeted exploration.
approach: Present DualGraph memory architecture separating what agent knows (Knowledge Graph storing fine-grained units) from how it writes (Outline Graph). Analyze KG topology with structural signals to generate targeted search queries.
contribution: DualGraph consistently outperforms state-of-the-art on four OEDR benchmarks in report depth, breadth, and factual grounding, reaching 53.08 RACE score on DeepResearch Bench. Ablations confirm dual-graph design's centrality.
